To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nutrient starvation triggers release of cytokines and chemotactic factors from cells, and these factors can promote the recruitment of immune cells, which may be relevant for cancer immunotherapy.
nutrient deprivation in cancer cells triggers a stress response that promotes the release of cytokines, which attract immune cells and promote tumor inflammation.
starvation stress in tumor cells induces secretion of cytokines and chemotaxis factors that promote inflammation and recruit immune cells to the tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of metabolic stress in the communication between tumor and immune cells.

understanding the mechanisms by which cells adapt to metabolic stress, which can be caused by nutrient deprivation and/or by the presence of antimetabolic agents, and how these adaptations can affect the communication between cells in the tumor microenvironment.
understanding how the immune system is affected by the metabolic status of tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the starvation stress response in tumor cells promotes the recruitment of immune cells to the tumor microenvironment.
the starvation of cancer cells leads to the secretion of cytokines and chemotactic molecules that recruit immune cells to the tumor microenvironment.
tumor cells, in response to nutrient deprivation, release a cocktail of cytokines and chemotactic factors that recruit immune cells to the tumor site.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tumor cells can sense the local environment and respond to the lack of nutrients by releasing factors that promote angiogenesis and attract innate immune cell populations.

starvation of cancer cells promotes the release of cytokines and chemotactic molecules that can recruit immune cells, and these factors may also be used by cancer cells to recruit immune cells to their vicinity.
starvation and antimetabolic stress induce cytokine secretion from tumor cells, which can promote tumor inflammation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when nutrients become limited, tumor cells sequester nutrients from their environment, which in turn leads to the release of cytokines and chemotactic factors that promote recruitment of immune cells, such that tumor cells may be able to evade immune surveillance.
nutrient stress is a potent stimulus for the release of cytokines and chemotactic signals that can attract immune cells and promote an inflammatory environment.
tumor cells, in the context of nutrient deprivation, secrete factors that can attract and activate innate immune cells, and that these signals can be modulated by targeting metabolic pathways.
